extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students (and instructors) working through Rudin's Chapter 6 (real analysis / Riemann and Riemann–Stieltjes integration)
extracted.subtask_description: Exercise statements, solution hints, and pedagogical guidance for Rudin's Chapter 6 on (Riemann and Riemann–Stieltjes) integration; intended to guide students in proving equivalences, integrability criteria, inequalities and constructions related to integrals and integrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.2:2 — Riemann integral via mesh→0 equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the definition of the Riemann integral as a limit over partitions whose mesh (||P|| = sup Δx_i) approaches 0 is equivalent to Rudin's definition. In part (a) if P* is a refinement obtained by adding a single point to P and |f(x)| ≤ M, show U(P*,f) − U(P,f) ≤ 2M||P|| (and similarly for lower sums). In part (b) show equivalence of (i) Rudin's integrability and (ii) the mesh-based condition: for every ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that every partition P of mesh < δ satisfies U(P,f) − L(P,f) < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion for (i)⇒(ii): Choose by (i) a partition P0 with upper−lower < ε/2; then for any partition P of sufficiently small mesh, use part (a) to show U(P∪P0,f)−L(P∪P0,f) differs from U(P,f)−L(P,f) by < ε/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:1 — Integral of 1 w.r.t. increasing α
rubrics_metrics.description: For any increasing function α on [a,b], show ∫_a^b 1 dα = α(b) − α(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the obvious formula and should follow from the definition of the Riemann–Stieltjes integral; note it could have been part of Theorem 6.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:2 — Functions 'mostly' zero have integral zero
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Let f be the Dirichlet-like function of 4:R18 taking 0 at irrationals and value 1/n at rationals with reduced form m/n; show f ∈ (α) and ∫_0^1 f dα = 0. (b) Show more generally that any f on [0,1] with the property that for every ε>0 the set {x∈[0,1]: |f(x)| ≥ ε} is finite satisfies ∫ f dα = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use the definition of the integral directly; for (b) reduce to finitely many nonzero points whose contribution vanishes under α if α is continuous increasing as in the exercise context.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:3 — Construct α increasing only on Cantor set
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a function α0 on the complement of the Cantor set by assigning constant values on the removed middle-thirds segments (1/2 on (1/3,2/3), 1/4 and 3/4 on the next stage segments, etc.), extend α0 to a continuous increasing α on [0,1]; then (b) show any continuous f zero on the Cantor set has ∫ f dα = 0; (c) give an example of such a nonzero f; (d) show if f and g are continuous and agree on Cantor set then ∫ f dα = ∫ g dα; (e)/(f) related examples and explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: use base-3 representation of x (change first '1' digit to '2', replace later digits with 0s, map 0/2 ternary digits to binary, etc.). Also show α0(x−) and α0(x+) exist and are equal to extend continuously. Use these constructs to deduce integrals vanish for functions supported off Cantor set.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:4 — Integrable composed with integrable need not be integrable
rubrics_metrics.description: Give an example demonstrating that if f and φ are Riemann-integrable functions, their composite φ ∘ f need not be Riemann-integrable (contrast to Theorem 6.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: let f be the function of 4:R18 (dense oscillation behavior) and pick φ discontinuous at the real number f most often approaches; choose φ discontinuous at that value. Examples exist even where f is continuous but composition fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:5 — Condition for increasing α to yield integrability of f
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove: if f is increasing and f is continuous at every point where α is discontinuous, then f ∈ (α) (i.e., f is Riemann–Stieltjes integrable w.r.t. α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine ideas from proofs of Theorems 6.8 and 6.9 and use exercise 4.3:5(a); exploit that the increments Δα_i are small where α is continuous and control contributions where α jumps.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:6 — Equivalent conditions for mutual integrability of α and β
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the three conditions of 6.2:1 are equivalent to: (iv) For every x∈[a,b), either α(x)=α(x+) or β(x)=β(x+); and for every x∈(a,b], either α(x)=α(x−) or β(x)=β(x−).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume (iv), let M = (α(b)+β(b))−(α(a)+β(a)). Given ε, find partition with each interval having either Δα_i or Δβ_i < ε/(2M); deduce bounds on Δα_i Δβ_i via (Δα_i+Δβ_i)(ε/(2M)) and sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.3:7 — Spotting a fallacy about continuity proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Find the fallacy in the bogus argument 'every function f:X→Y between metric spaces is continuous' that uses 'since ε is arbitrary' improperly; then explain why similar uses of 'ε is arbitrary' in proofs of Theorems 3.50 and 6.11 are valid and don't suffer the same fallacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare structure: the fallacy incorrectly lets choice of constants depend on points in a way invalidating the quantifier order; check quantifier order and dependence carefully in each valid proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:1 — Change-of-variable using inverse α when α strictly increasing
rubrics_metrics.description: If α is strictly increasing continuous on [a,b], it is a bijection onto [α(a),α(b)] with inverse α^−1. Show that for any real-valued function f on [a,b], ∫_a^b f(x) dα(x) = ∫_{α(a)}^{α(b)} f(α^−1(u)) du whenever either side is defined (equality of existence and values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is related to Theorem 6.19 but you may not use it in this part; argue by direct substitution and relation of partitions under α and its inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:2 — Functions behaving like zero under Riemann–Stieltjes integration
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If f∈(α) and ∫ f^2 dα = 0 then for all g∈(α) we have ∫ f g dα = 0. (b) If f∈(α) and f(x)≥0 then ∫ f dα = 0 is equivalent to ∫ f^2 dα = 0. (c) Variants where assumption f(x)≥0 is replaced by |f(x)| etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider (f + t g)^2 ≥ 0 and view the integral as a quadratic in t with a local minimum at t=0; expand and deduce relations. For (b) try to write f as a square of a function in (α) or use decomposition (|f|+f)/2 − (|f|−f)/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:3 — Schwarz (Cauchy–Schwarz) inequality for integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the Schwarz inequality for integrals (p= q = 2 case): for f,g∈(α), (∫ f g dα)^2 ≤ (∫ f^2 dα)(∫ g^2 dα).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimic the finite-dimensional proof using integrals in place of sums. Handle 'zero norm' cases (where some integrals of squares are zero) using 6.4:2.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:4 — Characterization of (α+β)
rubrics_metrics.description: If α and β are increasing on [a,b], show (α+β) (the class of functions integrable w.r.t α+β) equals (α) ∩ (β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show integrability with respect to α+β is equivalent to integrability with respect to each summand; use linearity and control of upper/lower sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:5 — Extend Riemann–Stieltjes integral to non-increasing λ
rubrics_metrics.description: If λ can be written λ = α1 − α2 with α1, α2 increasing and f integrable with respect to both, define ∫ f dλ = ∫ f dα1 − ∫ f dα2 and show this is independent of decomposition of λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show if λ = β1 − β2 is another decomposition, then I(α1,α2) = I(β1,β2) by manipulations such as I(α1,α2) = I(α1+β2, α2+β2) and similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:6 — Converse additivity for integrability over subintervals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a<c<b, α monotone increasing and f∈(α) on [a,c] and on [c,b], then f∈(α) on [a,b] and ∫_a^b f dα = ∫_a^c f dα + ∫_c^b f dα.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essentially verify additivity across a partition point c; the usual argument about upper and lower sums and refinements applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:7 — Integrable functions can have infinitely many large jumps
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct f on [a,b] piecewise linear between an increasing sequence s1<s2<... with s1=a and limit b, defining f(x) = (x−s_i)/(s_{i+1}−s_i) for x∈[s_i, s_{i+1}), f(b)=0; determine discontinuities and values of one-sided limits and show f∈L (Riemann integrable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (a) asks where f is discontinuous and the one-sided values; (b) deduces integrability using those properties (no proof required for (a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:8 — Integrability piece by piece (countable partitioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let s1<s2<... increase to b; let α be increasing and f bounded on [a,b]. Then f∈(α) iff for every i the restriction f_i on [s_i, s_{i+1}] is in (α_i) and the sum Σ ∫_{s_i}^{s_{i+1}} f dα is absolutely convergent; when true, ∫_a^b f dα equals that sum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write integrals as countable sum of integrals on subintervals; take care with absolute convergence and formal expression of ith summand.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:9 — Countable discontinuities imply integrability
rubrics_metrics.description: A bounded f on [a,b] that is continuous except at a countable set {s_i} is Riemann-integrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover each discontinuity s_i by a small neighborhood of length δ_i with Σ δ_i small; take finite subcovering and create partition as in (a) to control total length of intervals with large oscillation, mimicking the proof of Theorem 6.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:10 — Riemann-integrable function with uncountably many discontinuities (Cantor indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define f:[0,1]→R by f=1 on Cantor set and 0 elsewhere; show f is Riemann integrable despite being discontinuous on uncountably many points; determine its integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partitions into 3^n equal intervals and count those that contain a Cantor point; show proportion of intervals containing a Cantor point tends to 0 as n→∞, so integral is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:11 — One case of Theorem 6.12(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the last equation in Theorem 6.12(a) in the case c<0 (distinguish cases c>0 and c<0 when proving that equation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not hard; watch sign distinctions when handling c negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.4:12 — Theorem 6.11 for multivariable ϕ∘f
rubrics_metrics.description: Let α increasing on [a,b] and f = (f1,...,fk) with each fj∈(α). For a continuous ϕ on a compact K containing f([a,b]), prove ϕ∘f ∈(α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given ε>0 find δ so that |ϕ(p)−ϕ(q)|<ε for d(p,q)<δ. Choose partition P such that each fj oscillation < δ/k on most subintervals; split indices into A (where f variation small) and B (rest), bound contributions from both sets so U(P,α,ϕ∘f)−L(...)→0 as ε→0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.5:1 — Derive Fundamental Theorem from Theorem 6.17
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f be integrable on [a,b] and suppose there exists differentiable F with F'=f. Use Theorem 6.17 to derive the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus formula; extend to differences f=f1−f2 where each is a derivative of differentiable functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Theorem 6.17 with constant function 1 as 'f' and F as 'α' then use 6.3:1 for one side; handle decomposition f=f1−f2 and use scalar adjustments if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.5:2 — Strengthened Theorem 6.16 with weakened continuity assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Show Theorem 6.16 remains valid if f is only bounded and continuous at the specified points s_n rather than continuous everywhere: specifically verify display (24) remains valid and adapt the rest of the proof to conclude f∈(α) and formula (23) holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note no continuity is needed until display (24); justify that display under weaker assumptions and then adapt Rudin's proof (possibly using integrability of f wrt α2).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.5:3 — Decomposition of increasing α into jumps and continuous part
rubrics_metrics.description: Show every increasing α on [a,b] can be written α(x) = Σ c_n I(x−s_n) + Σ d_n J(x−s_n) + β(x), where Σ c_n and Σ d_n converge (nonnegative), {s_n} lists points of discontinuity, and β is continuous increasing. Deduce Theorem 6.9 remains valid if α is only required continuous at points where f is discontinuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose c_n,d_n to match jump sizes at discontinuities; approximate by finite partial sums to show monotonicity and continuity of β. Use J in place of I where appropriate and employ 6.5:2 variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.5:4 — Integration under reversal ρ(x)=−x
rubrics_metrics.description: Show identity ∫_{−b}^{−a} f(−x) d(−α(−x)) = ∫_a^b f(x) dα(x) (i.e., reversing variable and integrator behaves well), and deduce how to extend theorems proven for increasing α to decreasing α by sign changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ρ(x)=−x and rewrite integrals: ∫ (f∘ρ) d(ρ∘α∘ρ) = ∫ f dα. Then change 'increasing' to 'decreasing' by replacing β with −β in formulas as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:1 — Derivative formula for Riemann–Stieltjes integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: If α is strictly increasing and f continuous on [a,b], define F(x)=∫_a^x f(t) dα(t). Show the derivative dF/dα (i.e., lim_{t→x} (F(x)−F(t))/(α(x)−α(t))) exists and equals f(x) for all x∈[a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat α as new measure-like variable; continuity of f and strict monotonicity of α give the limit. This generalizes the usual FTC derivative formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:2 — Reduction of repeated integrals to single integral (convolution-type formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If f continuous on [a,b] show ∫_a^b (∫_a^t f(s) ds) f(t) dt = ∫_a^b (∫_a^t f(s) ds) f(t) dt = ∫_a^b (b−t) f(t) dt? (exercise asks to show equality of two iterated integrals by differentiating and comparing derivatives and values). (b) Generalize to n-fold iterated integrals. (c) Extend to merely Riemann-integrable f with some continuity at a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite with arbitrary x in place of b, name left P(x) and right Q(x); show both differentiable with same derivative hence equal up to constant; check endpoints to get equality. For noncontinuous cases, approximate and use derivative behavior at x0 using (x−x0)u(x) differentiability trick.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:3 — Fundamental Theorem without integrability of derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the inequality version: for any differentiable F on [a,b], ∫_a^b F'(x) dx ≤ F(b) − F(a) ≤ ∫_a^b F'(x) dx (upper and lower integrals used appropriately) — i.e., show bounds when F' might not be integrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt arguments of Theorem 6.21 to allow possible nonintegrability: compare upper and lower sums and use mean value-like estimates for increments of F.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:4 — Formal product law for d(αβ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f be a function and α,β monotonically increasing nonnegative functions on [a,b] with f ∈ (α)∩(β), α∈(β) and β∈(α). Prove ∫ f d(αβ) = ∫ f α dβ + ∫ f β dα (a generalization of integration by parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 6.2:1 style manipulations and linearity; interpret Δ(αβ) ≈ αΔβ + βΔα and pass to integrals via limits of Riemann–Stieltjes sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:5 — Repeated Riemann–Stieltjes integration (two-variable kernel)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Suppose α,β increasing with α∈(β) and f∈(α)∩(β). Show the function x ↦ ∫_a^x (∫_a^t f(s) dα(s)) dβ(t) equals ∫_a^x (β(b)−β(t)) f(t) dα(t) under positivity assumption and then in general. (b) Show for continuous u and v one can represent iterated integrals as ∫_a^x w(x,t) f(t) dt for some continuous kernel w(x,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For (a) consider the case where inner integral values have known extremes on intervals; for (b) first prove nonnegative case then extend via linearity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:6 — Characterization of Riemann–Stieltjes integral via primitive F
rubrics_metrics.description: Let α increasing and f bounded on [a,b]. Define F(x)=∫_a^x f dα. Then (i) F(a)=0 and (ii) for a≤x1<x2≤b, ΔF ∈ [(Δα)(inf_{[x1,x2]} f), (Δα)(sup_{[x1,x2]} f)]. Show conversely that any unique F satisfying (i) and (ii) yields f∈(α) and equals that integral; prove uniqueness and how upper/lower integrals bound F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show both the upper and lower integral functions F^+(x)=∫_a^x f^+ dα and F^− similarly satisfy the bounds, then uniqueness follows from sandwiching. For converse, construct upper and lower integrals and use the inequalities to deduce equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.6:7 — Change-of-variables for integrals with nonnegative weight g
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose α is monotonically increasing and f,g continuous on [a,b] with g nonnegative. Prove an identity relating nested integrals: an iterated integral involving f and g with respect to α can be transformed to a single integral of f·g with respect to α (exercise indicates a change-of-variables / Fubini-type rearrangement for this setting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 6.12 and monotonicity/nonnegativity of g to justify exchanging order or transforming the iterated integral; mimic standard proofs of integration-by-parts/change-of-order in the Riemann–Stieltjes setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6.7:1 — Integrability of vector-valued functions via partition diameters
rubrics_metrics.description: A function f:[a,b]→R^k is integrable w.r.t increasing α iff for every ε>0 there exists partition P such that Σ_{i=1}^n diam(f([x_{i−1},x_i])) Δα_i < ε. Moreover, given such P, any Riemann sum Σ f(t_i) Δα_i approximates the integral to within ε, and any refinement P* of P also satisfies the inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the diameter-based criterion (Definition 3.9) and mimic scalar proofs: small oscillation of vector-valued f on subintervals times Δα_i makes Riemann–Stieltjes sums close to the integral; show stability under refinements.
